name: あぶらそば 油珉 (Abura Soba Yumin)

claims.text: The bowls are abura soba dressed in an oil-and-tare sauce of the standard type, which is based on wheat-containing soy sauce; no wheat-free tare is offered.
Bowls are built on pork fat (背脂), fatty pork, eggs and mayo-based toppings shared across the kitchen; there is no plant-based bowl and no separation from animal ingredients.

name: 油そば 大革命 金閣寺店 (Aburasoba Daikakumei Kinkakuji-ten)

claims.text: The dish is built on a soy-sauce-based tare mixed through wheat noodles; standard Japanese soy sauce tare contains wheat, making the sauce as well as the noodles unsuitable for gluten avoidance.
Bowls center on pork (chashu / pork belly) and meat-miso, with karaage on set menus; the kitchen is meat-forward and offers no plant-based bowl.

name: あけてもくれても (Akete mo Kurete mo)

claims.text: The bowls are built on a sweet soy-based tare over wheat noodles, so wheat is present in both the seasoning and the noodles.
Pork-bone broth, large chashu, and pork back-fat are standard across the menu, with no meat-free preparation noted.

name: あきちゃんラーメン (Akichan Ramen)

claims.text: The chuka soba is seasoned with a sharp soy-and-salt tare typical of the style; soy sauce in Japanese ramen is normally wheat-based, so the broth should be assumed to contain wheat.
Broth is a pork-based clear consomme and bowls are topped with chashu pork belly, so all standard items contain animal products.
The dipping broth is a thick pork-bone-and-seafood tare-based tsukejiru, and the spicy version is miso-based (辛醤つけめん); these standard ramen/tsukemen seasonings contain wheat-based soy/miso.

name: 力餅食堂 柿仲 (Chikara Mochi Shokudo Kakichu)

claims.text: Wheat-noodle-centric diner (chūka soba, udon, soba) sharing one small kitchen; no gluten-free accommodation noted.
Signature bowl uses char siu pork, fish-cake kamaboko and a dashi-based broth; no plant-based preparation indicated.

name: 珍遊 一乗寺本店 (Chinyu Ichijoji Honten)

claims.text: The ramen uses a traditional soy-based (shoyu) tare, which in a shop of this style is wheat-based; no gluten-free tare or noodles are offered.
Broth is animal-based throughout — a chicken-bone stock enriched with pork back fat — so there is no non-animal stock prepared on site.

name: 珍遊 河原町六角店 (Chinyu Kawaramachi Rokkaku)

claims.text: Wheat ramen noodles are boiled in shared water and the broth/tare contain wheat-based shoyu; a shared ramen kitchen offers no gluten-free path or separation.
The tare is described as an aged/traditional soy sauce ('老舗の醤油でまろやかな風味に'), and Japanese brewed shoyu is almost always made with wheat — treat the seasoning as wheat-containing.
The base broth is chicken paitan (chicken bones, whole chicken, chicken feet) finished with animal back fat, so every bowl is animal-based with no plant-based stock available.
